transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CTO, Sable), Mei Chen (ML Eng, Sable), Samir Patel (Head of Platform, Sable)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i think we have priya from our solutions engineering team as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alex: hey jordan, doing well, excited to dig in. we chatted a bit in email - high-level goal is to pick a model and deployment strategy for our contextual retrieval + RAG product.
[00:14] Jordan: great - quick run through purpose: we want to understand your workloads (context length, languages, tool calls) and constraints (data residency, sla, cost) so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private and specific open-model choices. priya, anything to add?
[00:29] Priya: yeah, hi all. i'll focus on latency and perf implications - i want to capture sample token budgets, expected qps, and any special features like function calling or tool integration.
[00:39] Samir: sounds good. to start, our main product is a user-facing assistant that ingests long documents - legal contracts, multi-lingual customer support history - and we do retrieval over a vector DB, then pass long context to the model. we're seeing up to 40-60k tokens in worst-case contexts after concatenating retrieved docs.
[00:56] Mei: and we need robust multilingual handling - EN, ES, FR, PT, and occasionally ZH. tokenization differences matter for cost and perf.
[01:10] Jordan: okay that's helpful - so long-context is critical. are you currently running any models in prod?
[01:16] Alex: we have a small on-prem setup using an older Llama 2 13b fork for early testing, but perf and management have been a pain. looking at Redwood so we can scale more predictably and possibly avoid reinventing orchestration.
[01:27] Priya: quick clarifying q: for your 40-60k token contexts, is that mostly dense document concatenation or do you do selective summarization / condensation before sending?
[01:36] Samir: currently we do minimal condensation - we'd prefer the model handle more directly. but we want options: long-context models vs chunking + stitching.
[01:45] [02:00] Alex: also important - we have strict data residency for EU customers, so private deployment or dedicated in EU region might be required. SOC2 is a must.
[02:12] Jordan: absolutely. Redwood Private supports VPC / on-prem options; Dedicated can be provisioned in EU regions with contractual addenda. we are SOC2 compliant - i'll include the certs in follow up.
[02:23] Mei: thanks. on models specifically, we are comparing Llama 3-70B-like options, Mistral-Instruct, and some community 34/70b quantized variants. we also are worried about tool-calling / function calling support for structured DB calls. which models do you recommend for tool-calling?
[02:40] Priya: good question. function/tool calling support is model and runtime-dependent. on hosted Redwood we provide a model catalog with verified variants. For tool-calling, you want models trained or fine-tuned with instruction+structured output behavior - some Llama-derivatives and Mistral do a decent job. Additionally our runtime provides structured output helpers to help stabilize tool calls (e.g. JSON schema enforcement).
[03:02] Alex: is there a difference in term of latency and cost between using a 70b quantized model vs a 34b? we care about user-facing latency sub-800ms ideally.
[03:11] Priya: yes tradeoff: 70b (even quantized) tends to have higher per-token cost and higher latencies; however if you need longer context and better instruction-following it may be worth it. We often recommend 34b or 32k context 30-32k variants for a balance. For 50k-65k contexts, you may need specialized long-context models (and more memory), which typically run on multi-GPU shards or a dedicated node setup - which points to Dedicated or Private.
[03:41] [03:55] Samir: what about our desire for streaming partial outputs and tool calls mid-generation? we can't wait for full completion then parse.
[04:04] Priya: Redwood runtime supports streaming responses and staged tool calls; there's also a function-calling API where the model can emit a call event and we handle invocation. Some models are more reliable for mid-stream call behavior - we test them in our catalog. we'll share our model performance profiles.
[04:20] Alex: multilingual - is tokenization consistent across models? we noticed some models tokenize Chinese very inefficiently which spikes cost.
[04:28] Priya: tokenization varies; for Chinese you may want models with native CJK pretraining or specific tokenizer configs. we recommend running your multilingual corpus through candidate tokenizers - we can do that as part of the bench.
[04:42] Mei: excellent, please do. also curious about caching - KV cache and prefix caching - can Redwood help reduce repeated cost for similar prompts?
[04:52] Jordan: yes we have automatic prefix/KV caching and request-level caching for identical contexts; that often reduces per-token cost. Priya can show benchmarking examples.
[05:05] [05:20] Priya: i'll note: if you cache until the last user message, you'll hit gains for repeated retrieval queries. but for unique long documents caching is less effective unless you canonicalize the input.
[05:33] Alex: got it. another question: if we start hosted to move fast, can we later migrate to Dedicated or Private without changes to the app?
[05:40] Jordan: absolutely - that's one of Redwood's selling points: identical API and config layer across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. you'll be able to pin model versions and routing policies without app changes.
[05:53] Samir: what about SLA and tail latency - hosted doesn't give guarantees right?
[05:58] Jordan: hosted has best-effort latency. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and SLA-backed uptime/latency. Private gives full control for on-prem. If tail latency and contractual SLAs are important, Dedicated is the path.
[06:11] Mei: do you support KMS/HSM integrations for key management on Dedicated/Private? we require envelope encryption with customer-managed keys.
[06:18] Jordan: yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and HSM options for Private). audit logs and RBAC are available. i'll attach the security docs.
[06:28] [06:40] Alex: latency numbers for a 32k context 34b model - ballpark?
[06:45] Priya: ballpark depends heavily on batch size and QPS. single-shot with minimal batching on a modern GPU: 34b 32k context could be ~700-1200ms per response for a 1-2 second generation, but that's approximation. For 65k context models you'll typically see higher latency and often multi-second responses. We'll provide measured numbers from our catalog.
[07:06] Alex: ok thanks. are there known issues with tool-calls causing hallucinations with Llama variants?
[07:13] Priya: some models tend to be less deterministic for the exact JSON schema; we mitigate with schema-enforced decoding and a fallback verification step. For high reliability use cases we sometimes recommend a smaller specialized model fine-tuned for function-calls or running additional verification step in the pipeline.
[07:29] Mei: question on costs - do you charge per token for all deployment modes?
[07:34] Jordan: hosted is usage-based (per-token and per-embedding). Dedicated is typically reserved capacity (monthly commit) which is more predictable; Private is licensed + infra. We can run scenarios to map to your expected qps and token budgets.
[07:50] [08:05] Samir: what about model quantization and impact on accuracy for multilingual tasks? some quantized 4-bit modes degrade performance on low-resource languages.
[08:15] Priya: correct - quantization can affect quality, especially on complex multilingual tasks. our Optimize team provides recommendations on quantization profiles per model and workload; we'll propose a small test matrix.
[08:27] Alex: for the initial pilot we'd prefer hosted to avoid ops, but we'd like a path to Dedicated in EU if things look good. can we get a short pilot with 32k context models and tool-calling validation?
[08:39] Jordan: yes, we can do a hosted pilot focused on candidate models with an option to replicate the bench on Dedicated for an apples-to-apples comparison.
[08:49] Mei: please also test tokenizer cost for our Spanish/Portuguese/Chinese corpus and include token counts.
[08:58] Priya: will do. i'll run tokenizer pass and provide numbers.
[09:05] [09:20] Alex: any special infra needs for 65k contexts? you mentioned multi-gpu sharding - will that force dedicated?
[09:28] Priya: long-context 65k often needs model variants with longer sequence training and memory across multiple GPUs. Our Hosted can sometimes handle certain 65k-capable models but throughput will be limited; for production at scale Dedicated/Private with pinned GPU capacity is recommended.
[09:44] Jordan: to be concrete, for heavy 65k use you should anticipate a Dedicated node setup or Private cluster, particularly if you need strict regional residency.
[09:53] Samir: fine. a couple compliance q's - do you provide audit logs per request and integration with our SIEM?
[09:59] Jordan: yes audit logs are supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted provides limited logs but we can offer enhanced logging as an add-on. integrations with common SIEMs via syslog/ingestion are supported.
[10:12] [10:30] Mei: what's the expected time to migrate to Dedicated from hosted? we want a rough timeline.
[10:36] Jordan: usually 4-8 weeks from contract to provisioning for Dedicated (depends on region and capacity). Private on-prem takes longer. We'll scope during sales process.
[10:46] Alex: ok that's acceptable. one more item: we use tool-chains where the model calls internal microservices. how do you secure those invocations?
[10:55] Priya: tool invocation can be proxied through our control plane with credential injection and short-lived tokens; for Private deployments it can be done entirely within your network. we can show the flow in the deep dive.
[11:07] [11:30] Alex: great. any red flags for us?
[11:33] Priya: nothing major - main areas to validate: 1) model choice for long context + multilingual quality, 2) latency/cost tradeoffs for the expected qps, and 3) residency/SOC2 + KMS needs.
[11:46] Samir: we'll need to align internal stakeholders - security, legal, and our infra folks.
[11:51] Jordan: understood. i'll include a one-pager for the legal team and the SOC2 artifact.
[11:58] [12:15] Mei: can you send an example of the bench sheet so we can add our prompts?
[12:20] Priya: yes - link will be shared; it has templates for tokenizer pass, latency/cost rows, and expected outputs.
[12:30] Alex: perfect. to recap, we want: hosted pilot focused on 32k context models with tool-calling test, tokenizer counts for multi-lingual corpus, and a follow-up technical bench for Dedicated if numbers look promising.
[12:43] Jordan: sounds right - i'll send pricing and security docs, priya will run the initial bench and tokenizer pass. schedule the deeper bench next week.
[12:55] Samir: thanks everyone.
[13:00] Jordan: thanks all. meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attribution and minor mis-spellings (e.g., "K V cache" vs "KV cache"). Shared artifacts referenced: security-onepager.pdf (link), model-benchmarks.csv (link), tokenizer-pass-template.xlsx (link).
